text:
alex: FYI — customer (AcmeMaps) reports duplicate completions + double billing after SSE disconnect & fast reconnect. They saw the same final text twice in the transcript and were billed twice. Repro steps attached. @jamie could you triage? :eyes:

jamie: On it. Can you paste the raw stream ids + client logs? Which SDK/version?

alex: logs below. client: acme-sdk-js v2.1.4. root stream id: s_8a3f, session_id: sess-197, resume_token changes every reconnect. snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T12:01:23.321Z] SSE disconnect code=1006
[2026-03-10T12:01:23.450Z] reconnect -> resume_token=rtk-71
[2026-03-10T12:01:23.452Z] POST /v1/stream ... idempotencyKey=null
[2026-03-10T12:01:23.600Z] client received chunk part_id=chunk-4/last=true text="...final"
[2026-03-10T12:01:23.601Z] client ACK resume_token=rtk-71
```

olivia: interesting — no idempotency key in POST, so server treats reconnect as a fresh request. But why double text? maybe resume applied but server also re-ran generation. Do we have server-side request ids / job ids?

jamie: attaching server trace: job_id j-5f2, request_id r-990. Looks like worker wrote partial chunk to stream, then resumed and re-executed because resume token check hit a race while kvcache persisted. trace:
```
[worker j-5f2] emit chunk chunk-4 seq=37 partial=true
[router] resume token rtk-70 invalidated -> accept new request
[worker j-5f2] generation completed, wrote final output
```

alex: Customer says reconnect latency was 120ms — very fast. Could be replay + resumed generation overlap.

jamie: Hypothesis: when reconnect is fast, client opens new request without idempotency key; server resume logic allowed both: the in-flight generation completed and also the new request executed producing the same completion — dup shown and billed twice. We need to decide: patch server to enforce resume vs new-request dedupe using session_id + last_chunk_id, and recommend idempotencyKey in SDK.

olivia: short-term mitigation: advise customer to set idempotencyKey per initial request; SDK patch to automatically reuse idempotencyKey across reconnects. Also recommend client wait ~300ms before issuing a new POST when resume token rotates.

support-mgr: draft reply to customer:
"Thanks — we believe a race between fast reconnect + missing idempotency key caused duplicate generation and billing. Engineering is deploying a server-side guard; in the meantime please upgrade to acme-sdk-js >=2.1.6 (auto idempotency) or set an idempotencyKey. We'll credit the duplicate tokens."

jamie: created issue INF-3412, will land guard: drop re-exec of request if session_id matches and last_emitted_chunk_id >= incoming_resume_offset. Rolling canary to 5% now.

eng-oncall-bot: deploy INF-3412 -> canary-5% started 2026-03-10T14:05:00Z :rocket:

alex: great. I'll send customer the credit and repro steps; keep me posted if canary detects regressions. :thumbsup:
